title: Raw scalar localization preserves supported adjunctions and unique triangle maps
statement:
Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\mathcal T_X,\mathcal T_Z,\mathcal T_U$ be linear triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-linear-functor], with exact linear functors $i_*,i^*,i^!,j^*,j_*$ and adjunctions $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv i^!$ and $j^*\dashv j_*$. Assume $i^*i_*\to1$ and $j^*j_*\to1$ are invertible, $j^*i_*=0$, and for each $K\in\mathcal T_X$ the exceptional counit $e_K:i_*i^!K\to K$ and the open unit $u_K:K\to j_*j^*K$ are the first two arrows of a distinguished triangle $i_*i^!K\xrightarrow{e_K}K\xrightarrow{u_K}j_*j^*K\xrightarrow{\delta_K}i_*i^!K[1]$ (a supported triangle). Units and counits are required to commute with the supplied exact shifts.
Take the raw scalar localizations $\mathcal T_T[1/\varpi]$, whose objects are unchanged and whose Hom groups are tensored over $R$ with $E$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The localized exact functors carry the localized adjunctions, including their units, counits and shift structures; the supported triangles remain distinguished, and closed-to-open orthogonality holds in all shifts. In each original or localized category, for every $f:K\to L$ there is exactly one morphism between the supported triangles with middle component $f$. Its closed and open components are $i_*i^!f$ and $j_*j^*f$. In particular the connecting arrow is uniquely determined by $e_K,u_K$, and these arrows form a natural shift-compatible family.
For a separated finite-type scheme over a field in which $\ell$ is invertible, the identification of the completed integral constructible category with the stratified-perfect category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] induces an identification of these raw localizations, with the same objects and the same maps $h\otimes a$. Thus the assertion applies to the specified rational $D^b_c(-,E)$ without an idempotent completion. The exact structure on an integral kernel right adjoint may be the unique adjunction-compatible shift structure of the right adjoint of an exact functor; coefficient linearity is induced by the linear Hom adjunction. Moreover $i^!j_*G=0$ for every $G$, and the adjunction unit $Q\to i^!i_*Q$ is invertible in both the original and localized categories.

proof.text: If an integral kernel right adjoint is initially supplied only as an ordinary right adjoint, give it the unique adjunction-compatible coherent shifts of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. The left adjoint is exact, so [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] makes this right adjoint exact for those shifts. Its coefficient linearity follows from [lem-sbc-linear-right-adjoint]. More explicitly, for $F\dashv G$, the transpose $h\mapsto G(h)\eta_P$ and its inverse $a\mapsto\varepsilon_KF(a)$ are $R$-linear because $F,G$ are linear and composition is bilinear. Thus the supplied Hom adjunctions are linear, not merely bijections of sets. Apply this to $i_*\dashv i^!$; the other functors and shifts are already supplied.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact; linear Hom formulas and kernel-adjoint refinement of the item

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] for the three raw localized categories and their exact localization functors. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] with $S=R$, $u=t=\varpi$ and $\phi=1_R$ to each supplied functor and to its unit, counit and shift comparisons. The functor acts by $F_E(h\otimes a)=F(h)\otimes a$, and the transformations have components $\eta_P\otimes1$, $\varepsilon_K\otimes1$. For every adjoint pair, the two triangle identities remain identities: each is a well-typed equation of whiskerings and composites preserved by that lemma. Hence these are adjunctions with exactly the localized unit and counit. Their Hom bijections are the tensor extensions of the two inverse linear maps of step 1, so remain inverse without any finite-generation assumption. Shift-compatibility equations are preserved by the same lemma, as are the inverse equations for $i^*i_*\to1$ and $j^*j_*\to1$. The image of each given supported triangle is distinguished, and its first two arrows are precisely the new exceptional counit and open unit.

source.place: Rational stage: exact linear functor, adjunction data and triangle maps rationalize

proof.text:
In the original category, for $P\in\mathcal T_Z$, $N\in\mathcal T_U$ and $m,n\in\mathbf Z$, exactness of $i_*,j_*$ and $j^*\dashv j_*$ give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],j_*N[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[m],N[n])=0,$$
since $j^*i_*P=0$. The localized group is this zero module tensored with $E$, hence zero, by [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Thus all the required orthogonality groups vanish in both categories; no faithfulness of scalar localization is assumed. The isomorphism $i^*i_*\to1$ makes $i_*$ fully faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-counit-iso-right-fully-faithful]. Consequently the unit $Q\to i^!i_*Q$ is invertible by [lem-sp-adjunction-unit-fully-faithful-left]. Apply these two results also to the localized adjunctions, whose counit remains invertible by step 2.

source.place: Vanishing, rational Hom tensor formula, and Consequences: closed adjunction unit

proof.text:
Work in either category and write $A_K=i_*i^!K$ and $B_K=j_*j^*K$. Naturality gives $fe_K=e_L(i_*i^!f)$ and $(j_*j^*f)u_K=u_Lf$. The vanishing in step 3 includes $\operatorname{Hom}(A_K[1],B_L)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension](2) to the distinguished supported triangles for $K,L$: the two displayed squares therefore extend to a morphism of triangles and determine its first and third components uniquely. Its middle component is $f$, so the last square is
$$\delta_L(j_*j^*f)=(i_*i^!f)[1]\delta_K.$$
The same node's clause (3), using $\operatorname{Hom}(A_K[1],B_K)=0$, gives uniqueness of the connecting map for the fixed first two arrows. Identities and composites of these triangle maps have their prescribed middle components, so uniqueness also proves functoriality.

Shift the supported triangle three times by rotation (TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category]); its arrows are $-e_K[1],-u_K[1],-\delta_K[1]$. Changing the signs of the first and third vertices gives the isomorphic distinguished triangle with arrows $e_K[1],u_K[1],-\delta_K[1]$. The supplied adjunction-compatible shifts identify its first two arrows with $e_{K[1]},u_{K[1]}$. The connecting-map uniqueness of step 4 therefore identifies $\delta_{K[1]}$ with $-\delta_K[1]$ under those comparisons. Iterating and shifting backwards gives the usual $(-1)^n$ rule for every integer $n$. This is the signed shift compatibility of the connecting family; it is not an unsigned equality. Finally, for $H=i^!j_*G$, adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(H,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*H,j_*G)=0$ by step 3. Hence $1_H=0$, which makes $H$ a zero object: every arrow to or from $H$ factors through its zero identity. This proves $i^!j_*G=0$ before and after localization.

source.place: Vanishing and uniqueness; Consequences: exceptional pullback of an open direct image

proof.text: Let $T$ be a separated finite-type scheme over the stated field. Its base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0,k$ and its spectrum has one point), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. It is finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and $\ell$ is invertible by hypothesis. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] are thus satisfied. That statement identifies the completed integral category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform reduction bounds, with the stratified-perfect category and with [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], over the same completed ring sheaf and with the same reductions. These are full subcategories with exactly the same objects in the same ambient derived category. Their identification is therefore the identity on objects and Hom modules, rather than a new realization equivalence.

source.place: Propositions 6.6.11 and 6.8.11(3); the explicit comparison node retains the DAG witness and uniformity conditions

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], raw rationalization keeps objects and replaces every Hom module $M$ by $M\otimes_RE$. Apply this to the identity identification of step 6: it is again the identity on objects and sends $h\otimes a$ to the very same $h\otimes a$. Composition, shifts and the distinguished triangles agree because their integral data agree. Thus the results of steps 1–5 apply to the specified rational $D^b_c(-,E)$, with no idempotents adjoined.
